prompt: Вот у меня текст лекций по теории вероятностей (вытащил из PDF, распознавание местами кривое, файл case4-lecture-notes.txt лежит в этой папке) и официальный список экзаменационных билетов от кафедры (case4-tickets-list.txt, тоже здесь). Экзамен устный, строго по этим 5 билетам. Помоги подготовиться с нуля — хочу, чтобы билеты в итоге были оформлены как экзаменационные карточки для тренировки, а не просто лежали текстом.
fixture: No prior state (fresh learner). Two plain-text input files: lecture notes covering 4 of the 5 official tickets in some depth, and the official 5-ticket exam list from the department (authority: official_exam_list, outranks lecture_notes). Ticket 5 (independence of random variables) has NO corresponding lecture-notes coverage — an intentional source-coverage gap.
targets: load materials from scratch and reach a state where the tickets exist as structured, individually practiceable assessment records ('minted'), not just prose

assertions.text: The tutor reads both provided files in full before proposing anything.
assertions.rationale: Any competent assistant given two named files and a task referencing them will read both; likely to pass in both configurations.

assertions.text: The tutor treats the official department ticket list as authoritative over the lecture notes, and specifically surfaces that ticket 5 (independence of random variables) has no matching lecture-notes coverage instead of silently inventing content for it.
assertions.rationale: This requires the explicit source-authority-order and coverage-gap-reporting behavior documented in SKILL.md/source-of-truth.md; a generalist baseline has no equivalent policy and is likely to either merge everything unremarked or invent plausible probability-theory content for ticket 5 on its own general knowledge, which is exactly the silent-substitution failure mode being tested for.

assertions.text: The five tickets end up represented as structured, individually addressable practice records (each with its own prompt/id that could be drawn later for a specific ticket) rather than only as a single prose document or a flat set of notes.
assertions.rationale: This is literally the CLI's mint-assessments/freeze-assessment concept; nothing generic would produce an equivalent structured, re-drawable artifact without the skill's protocol.

assertions.text: Before treating the proposed curriculum as final, some explicit validation/check step happens (not a silent, unchecked write of hand-authored targets).
assertions.rationale: Tests the validate-curriculum-before-apply-curriculum discipline the skill mandates; a baseline has no such two-step discipline to follow.

assertions.text: The tutor's reply to the learner is honest about what's ready and what (if anything, e.g. the ticket-5 coverage gap) still needs the learner's input, rather than claiming full completion regardless.
assertions.rationale: Depends on assertion 2 actually having surfaced the gap in the first place.
